title: Expose client IPs/ports in API
body:
I could be missing something, but right now there doesn't seem to be a way to get the address/port of a connected client from a server instance.

Are there any concerns about adding ```netcode_address_t``` to the API and adding a method like ```netcode_address_t netcode_server_client_address(int client_index)``` that returns the appropriate entry from ```netcode_server_t::client_address```?

nodes.body:
I don't want to expose the netcode_address_t as a public interface. This was an intentional design decision to keep the API simple and easy portable across different languages.

To do this, you'll see the public API of netcode.io passes all address data as strings instead.

So if you want to add a function that returns the client address as a string, I'm OK with that.

cheers

Ah, that makes sense! I'm fairly new to network programming and wasn't sure if there was a security issue to worry about. :)

I had actually added ```void netcode_server_client_address(struct netcode_server_t * server, int client_index, char* client_address);``` in my fork. Since it's so straightforward I'm not sure if it's worth submitting a pull request, but I can do that if you want.

Cheers, Dario
